chapters.screen: Decision Tree. A tree prices a home by asking yes/no questions about income. Watch it grow one split at a time, always choosing the cut that reduces squared error the most, until the curve becomes a staircase.
chapters.spoken: Decision Tree. A tree prices a home by asking yes-or-no questions about income. Watch it grow one split at a time, always choosing the cut that reduces squared error the most, until the curve becomes a staircase.

chapters.screen: Each dot is one California district: median income (x) and median house value (y). Showing 900 of the 12,384 districts the model trains on.
chapters.spoken: Each dot is one California district: median income and median house value. Showing 900 of the 12,384 districts the model trains on.

chapters.screen: Before any split the tree is a single leaf: it predicts the average price for every district. The red lines show how wrong that is.
chapters.spoken: Before any split the tree is a single leaf: it predicts the average price for every district. The red lines show how wrong that is.

chapters.screen: Each frame adds one split: the income cut that lowers the total squared error the most. Every leaf predicts the mean price of the training districts inside it.
chapters.spoken: Each frame adds one split: the income cut that lowers the total squared error the most. Every leaf predicts the mean price of the training districts inside it.

chapters.screen: 14 leaves: train RMSE $82k, validation $83k. Each step of the staircase is one leaf.
chapters.spoken: 14 leaves: train root mean squared error 82 thousand dollars, validation 83 thousand dollars. Each step of the staircase is one leaf.

chapters.screen: The unseen district follows the yes/no questions from the root down to one leaf. Its prediction is that leaf's average training price.
chapters.spoken: The unseen district follows the yes-or-no questions from the root down to one leaf. Its prediction is that leaf's average training price.

chapters.screen: Final exam: the trained model prices all 4,128 test districts it has never seen, a batch at a time. The map shows where it misses: blue = worth more than predicted.
chapters.spoken: Final exam: the trained model prices all 4,128 test districts it has never seen, a batch at a time. The map shows where it misses: blue means worth more than predicted.

chapters.screen: A tree cuts the floor into rectangles and gives each one a flat height, so the sheet is a set of flat terraces. Same algorithm, now given house age as well as income; height is its predicted price.
chapters.spoken: A tree cuts the floor into rectangles and gives each one a flat height, so the sheet is a set of flat terraces. Same algorithm, now given house age as well as income; height is its predicted price.

chapters.screen: Seven more inputs cut the typical error from $83k to $76k.
chapters.spoken: Seven more inputs cut the typical error from 83 thousand dollars to 76 thousand dollars.

chapters.screen: A tree splits the input into boxes and predicts each box's average: greedy, readable, and blind to anything between its split points. Limitation: predictions are flat steps, so two districts on either side of a split get very different prices, and deep trees memorise noise.
chapters.spoken: A tree splits the input into boxes and predicts each box's average: greedy, readable, and blind to anything between its split points. Limitation: predictions are flat steps, so two districts on either side of a split get very different prices, and deep trees memorise noise.
